claim: PKCθ is a critical mediator of signaling by the T cell antigen receptor and the principal costimulatory receptor CD28.
source: The protein kinase PKCθ is a critical mediator of signaling by the T cell antigen receptor and the principal costimulatory receptor CD28.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about PKCθ function.

claim: PKCθ selectively inactivates Coronin 1A at the center of the T cell interface with the antigen presenting cell.
source: PKCθ selectively inactivates the negative regulator of F-actin generation, Coronin 1A, at the center of the T cell interface with the antigen presenting cell (APC).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing PKCθ-dependent phosphorylation and localization of Coronin 1A.

claim: PKCθ-mediated inactivation of Coronin 1A allows for effective generation of the large actin-based lamellum required for recruitment of ADAM10.
source: This allows for effective generation of the large actin-based lamellum required for recruitment of the Notch-processing membrane metalloproteinase ADAM10.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data showing ADAM10 recruitment to the lamellum in Tg4WT but not Tg4KO cells.

claim: Enhancement of Notch activation by PKCθ is critical for efficient T cell proliferation and Th17 differentiation.
source: Such enhancement of Notch activation is critical for efficient T cell proliferation and Th17 differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing reduced proliferation and Th17 differentiation in PKCθ-deficient cells that is rescued by NICD overexpression.

claim: Notch family proteins are large, heterodimeric transmembrane receptors.
source: Notch family proteins are large, heterodimeric transmembrane receptors.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Notch protein structure.

claim: Upon Notch ligation by a Notch ligand, ADAM10 or ADAM17 removes the Notch extracellular domain.
source: Upon Notch ligation by one of a family of Notch ligands (Osborne and Minter, 2007), a plasma membrane-tethered matrix metalloproteinase, ADAM10 or ADAM17, removes the Notch extracellular domain.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and represents established knowledge of Notch processing.

claim: The γ-secretase complex liberates the Notch intracellular domain (NICD) after ADAM-mediated cleavage.
source: Subsequently, the plasma membrane-embedded γ-secretase complex liberates the Notch intracellular domain (NICD).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Notch signaling pathway.

claim: The NICD constitutively translocates to the nucleus where it displaces transcriptional repressors and recruits enhancers.
source: The NICD constitutively translocates to the nucleus where it displaces transcriptional repressors and recruits enhancers to genomic loci characterized by binding of the transcription factor RPBJκ (Borggrefe and Oswald, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents established knowledge of NICD function.

claim: Notch1 plays an essential role in T cell thymic development.
source: An essential role for Notch1 in T cell thymic development is well established (Robey et al., 1996; Washburn et al., 1997)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A Notch1 deficient hematopoietic compartment yields no T cells.
source: a Notch1 deficient hematopoietic compartment yields no T cells (Radtke et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Notch1 is activated following TCR stimulation.
source: Notch1 is activated following TCR stimulation (Amsen et al., 2004; Guy et al., 2013; Ong et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Notch1 is required for effector cell development.
source: and is required for effector cell development (Amsen et al., 2004; Keerthivasan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The degree of Notch1 activation is directly proportional to the strength of the TCR signal.
source: The degree of Notch1 activation is directly proportional to the strength of the TCR signal (Guy et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PKCθ integrates TCR and CD28 signals.
source: PKCθ, a serine/threonine kinase integrating TCR and CD28 signals (Altman and Kong, 2016)
evidence: This is supported by citation and represents established knowledge.

claim: PKCθ-deletion renders peripheral T cells hyporesponsive but allows normal thymic selection.
source: PKCθ-deletion renders peripheral T cells hyporesponsive but allows normal thymic selection (Sun et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Tg4 CD4+ T cells recognize the acetylated N-terminal peptide of myelin basic protein Ac1-9[4K] and its high affinity MHC-binding analogue Ac1-9[4Y].
source: Tg4 CD4+ T cells (Liu et al., 1995) recognize the acetylated N-terminal peptide of myelin basic protein Ac1-9[4K] and its high affinity MHC-binding analogue Ac1-9[4Y].
evidence: This is supported by citation and describes the experimental system used.

claim: NICD expression and changes thereof upon cellular activation were similar in Tg4 thymocytes, naïve and primed T cells.
source: NICD expression and changes thereof upon cellular activation were similar (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Notch activation was impaired in mature T cells from Tg4KO mice.
source: However, Notch activation was impaired in mature T cells from Tg4KO mice.
evidence: This is supported by multiple experimental approaches shown in Figure 1.

claim: Tg4KO mice showed reduced Notch1 expression sixteen hours after in vivo T cell activation by injecting mice with 80 µg [4Y] peptide s.c.
source: Tg4KO mice showed reduced Notch1 expression sixteen hours after in vivo T cell activation by injecting mice with 80 µg [4Y] peptide s.c. (Figure 1A,B)
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: Tg4KO mice were grossly normal with a reduced number and proportion of CD4+ splenocytes but unaffected Tg4 TCR expression.
source: even though Tg4KO mice were grossly normal with a reduced number and proportion of CD4+ splenocytes but unaffected Tg4 TCR expression (Figure 2A; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Reduced Notch expression in Tg4KO cells was confirmed by Western blot analysis 60 min after s.c. administration of [4Y] peptide.
source: Reduced Notch expression was confirmed by Western blot analysis 60 min after s.c. administration of [4Y] peptide (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Reduced Notch expression in Tg4KO cells was confirmed through analysis of Notch1-dependent hes1 expression.
source: and through analysis of Notch1-dependent hes1 expression (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Notch1 cleavage in naïve CD4+ T cells from PKCθ-deficient B10.PL mice was diminished following overnight activation with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28.
source: Corroborating these data in non-TCR transgenic T cells, Notch1 cleavage in naïve CD4+ T cells (CD4+, CD44−, CD25−) from PKCθ-deficient B10.PL mice was diminished following overnight activation with anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Notch activation is CD28-dependent.
source: Such Notch activation was CD28-dependent (Figure 1F), consistent with an important role of PKCθ downstream of CD28 (Huang et al., 2002; Kong et al., 2011; Yokosuka et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1F and citations to prior work.

claim: PKCθ-dependent Notch activation can occur within 5 to 20 min after T cell activation.
source: Increased nuclear Notch enrichment could be detected 5 to 20 min after in vitro T cell activation or after injecting mice with 80 µg [4Y] peptide s.c. (Figure 1G–I).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G-I.

claim: PKCθ-dependent Notch activation was corroborated using the 5C.C7 TCR transgenic system.
source: This effect was corroborated using a second TCR transgenic system, 5C.C7 (Singleton et al., 2009) (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1J and citation to prior work describing the system.

claim: T cell proliferation was defective in Tg4KO T cells.
source: In accordance with published data (Keerthivasan et al., 2011; Marsland et al., 2004; Tan et al., 2006), T cell proliferation, CD69 and c-Myc upregulation were defective in Tg4KO T cells whereas IL-2 was unaffected (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data in Figure 2B and citations to prior work.

claim: CD69 upregulation was defective in Tg4KO T cells.
source: In accordance with published data (Keerthivasan et al., 2011; Marsland et al., 2004; Tan et al., 2006), T cell proliferation, CD69 and c-Myc upregulation were defective in Tg4KO T cells whereas IL-2 was unaffected (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2C and citations to prior work.

claim: c-Myc upregulation was defective in Tg4KO T cells.
source: In accordance with published data (Keerthivasan et al., 2011; Marsland et al., 2004; Tan et al., 2006), T cell proliferation, CD69 and c-Myc upregulation were defective in Tg4KO T cells whereas IL-2 was unaffected (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2D and citations to prior work.

claim: IL-2 expression was unaffected in Tg4KO T cells.
source: In accordance with published data (Keerthivasan et al., 2011; Marsland et al., 2004; Tan et al., 2006), T cell proliferation, CD69 and c-Myc upregulation were defective in Tg4KO T cells whereas IL-2 was unaffected (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data in Figure 2D and citations to prior work.

claim: Tg4KO T cells showed no defect in Th1 cell differentiation.
source: Tg4KO T cells showed no defect in Th1 cell differentiation (Figure 2E–G).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular cytokine staining data shown in Figure 2E-G.

claim: The proportion of IL-17A+ T cells was significantly reduced in Tg4KO cells under conditions favoring Th17 development.
source: Conversely, the proportion of IL-17A+ T cells was significantly reduced under conditions favoring Th17 development (Figure 2H–J).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular cytokine staining data shown in Figure 2H-J.

claim: Overexpression of NICD in Tg4KO cells led to restoration of T cell proliferation.
source: Overexpression of NICD at 18.5 ± 1.5 fold the level in non-activated primed Tg4WT cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) so as to constitutively activate Notch in Tg4KO cells led to restoration of T cell proliferation (Figure 2K)
evidence: This is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 2K.

claim: Overexpression of NICD in Tg4KO cells led to restoration of Th17 cell differentiation.
source: Overexpression of NICD at 18.5 ± 1.5 fold the level in non-activated primed Tg4WT cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) so as to constitutively activate Notch in Tg4KO cells led to restoration of T cell proliferation (Figure 2K), Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A secretion (Figure 2L–N).
evidence: This is supported by intracellular cytokine staining data shown in Figure 2L-M.

claim: Overexpression of NICD in Tg4KO cells led to restoration of IL-17A secretion.
source: Overexpression of NICD at 18.5 ± 1.5 fold the level in non-activated primed Tg4WT cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D) so as to constitutively activate Notch in Tg4KO cells led to restoration of T cell proliferation (Figure 2K), Th17 cell differentiation and IL-17A secretion (Figure 2L–N).
evidence: This is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 2N.

claim: Notch1 enhances T cell proliferation and differentiation downstream of PKCθ.
source: Notch1 thus enhances T cell proliferation and differentiation downstream of PKCθ.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue experiments showing NICD overexpression restores function in PKCθ-deficient cells.

claim: ADAM10-GFP was recruited rapidly and transiently to the interface of Tg4WT T cells and APC.
source: ADAM10-GFP was recruited rapidly and transiently to the interface of Tg4WT T cells and APC (Figure 3A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Video 1) consistent with previous work in AND T cells (Guy et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A,B and Video 1, and citation to prior work.

claim: ADAM10-GFP was not enriched at the interface of Tg4KO T cells.
source: In contrast, ADAM10-GFP was not enriched at the interface of Tg4KO T cells (Figure 3A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Video 2).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A,B and Video 2.

claim: In Tg4WT cells, ADAM10 was enriched in the interface lamellum.
source: In Tg4WT cells, ADAM10 was enriched in the interface lamellum, an actin-based signaling structure (Roybal et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data and citation to prior work describing the lamellum.

claim: Impairment of lamellum formation with 40 nM Jasplakinolide prevented ADAM10 interface recruitment.
source: Impairment of lamellum formation with 40 nM Jasplakinolide (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) (Roybal et al., 2015a) prevented ADAM10 interface recruitment (Figure 3A,B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3A,B and citation to prior work.

claim: Impairment of lamellum formation with Jasplakinolide prevented Notch cleavage following stimulation with anti-CD3/28.
source: and Notch cleavage following stimulation with anti-CD3/28 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The defect in lamellal ADAM10 recruitment upon PKCθ-deficiency was selective since the lamellal accumulation of Themis was only moderately impaired.
source: The defect in lamellal ADAM10 recruitment upon PKCθ-deficiency was selective since the lamellal accumulation of Themis, a protein with substantially more prominent and persistent lamellal accumulation than ADAM10, was only moderately impaired (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-E.

claim: Actin-dependent ADAM10 recruitment to the T cell:APC interface at the early peak of T cell signaling activity mediates efficient Notch1 activation downstream of PKCθ.
source: Together, these data suggest that actin-dependent ADAM10 recruitment to the T cell:APC interface at the early peak of T cell signaling activity mediates efficient Notch1 activation downstream of PKCθ.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on ADAM10 recruitment, actin dependence, and Notch activation.

claim: Tg4KO T cells formed tight cell couples upon APC contact with a slightly reduced frequency compared to Tg4WT T cells (30 ± 5% versus 50 ± 4%, p=0.02).
source: Tg4KO T cells, whether transduced to express ADAM10-GFP or other sensors, formed tight cell couples upon APC contact albeit with a slightly reduced frequency compared to Tg4WT T cells (30 ± 5% versus 50 ± 4%, p=0.02)
evidence: This is supported by quantification of live cell imaging experiments.

claim: Coronin1A inhibits the Arp2/3 complex.
source: Coronin1A inhibits the Arp2/3 complex (Humphries et al., 2002; Oku et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Coronin regulates clearance of actin from the NK immune synapse.
source: and regulates clearance of actin from the NK immune synapse (Mace and Orange, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Coronin is an established interactor with and substrate of PKC.
source: Furthermore, Coronin is an established interactor with and substrate of PKC (Cai et al., 2005; Siegmund et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Coronin1A was highly enriched at the interface of Tg4WT and Tg4KO T cells.
source: Coronin1A was highly enriched at the interface of Tg4WT and Tg4KO T cells (Figure 4A,B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A; Videos 5 and 6).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 4A,B and Videos 5 and 6.

claim: Coronin1A spreading to the interface periphery was delayed in Tg4KO cells, leaving substantially more Coronin 1A in the lamellum.
source: Similar to actin, Coronin1A spreading to the interface periphery was delayed in Tg4KO cells, leaving substantially more Coronin 1A in the lamellum.
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The spatiotemporal distribution of Cofilin was unaffected by PKCθ deficiency.
source: As a specificity control, the spatiotemporal distribution of the dominant F-actin severing protein Cofilin (Roybal et al., 2016; Singleton et al., 2011) was unaffected by PKCθ deficiency (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and citations to prior work.

claim: Treating Tg4WT T cells with PMA and Calyculin A resulted in a shift in the ratio of phosphorylated to non-phosphorylated Coronin1A from 0.3 ± 0.1 to 2.8 ± 1.1 fold.
source: Treating Tg4WT T cells with PMA and Calyculin A resulted in a shift in the ratio of phosphorylated to non-phosphorylated Coronin1A from 0.3 ± 0.1 to 2.8 ± 1.1 fold, indicative of efficient Coronin1A phosphorylation (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by Phos-tag Western blot data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: The shift in phosphorylated to non-phosphorylated Coronin1A upon PMA and Calyculin A treatment was significantly smaller in Tg4KO cells (0.25 ± 0.05 to 0.8 ± 0.25 fold).
source: This shift was significantly (p<0.05) smaller in Tg4KO cells (0.25 ± 0.05 to 0.8 ± 0.25 fold) (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This is supported by Phos-tag Western blot data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: PKCθ is required for efficient PMA-induced phosphorylation of Coronin1A.
source: demonstrating that PKCθ is required for efficient PMA-induced phosphorylation of Coronin1A.
evidence: This is inferred from the reduced Coronin1A phosphorylation in Tg4KO cells.

claim: In Tg4WT T cells PKCθ inactivates Coronin 1A selectively in the region of most intense stimulating signaling.
source: Together, our data suggest (Figure 4E) that in Tg4WT T cells PKCθ (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B; Video 7) inactivates Coronin 1A selectively in the region of most intense stimulating signaling, i.e. the center of the T cell:APC interface with effects extending across the entire lamellum but not reaching the peripheral actin ring.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on PKCθ localization and Coronin1A phosphorylation and distribution.

claim: PKCθ locally inhibits Coronin 1A-mediated attenuation of actin dynamics, promoting the formation of a strong actin-based lamellum.
source: Thus PKCθ locally inhibits Coronin 1A-mediated attenuation of actin dynamics, promoting the formation of a strong actin-based lamellum.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on PKCθ, Coronin1A, and actin dynamics.

claim: PKCθ-mediated local inhibition of Coronin 1A allows for the efficient actin-driven recruitment of ADAM10 to the T cell:APC interface.
source: With regard to Notch1 activation this allows for the efficient actin-driven recruitment of ADAM10 to the T cell:APC interface.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on actin, ADAM10 recruitment, and Notch activation.

claim: The mechanism of enhanced Notch processing peaks within the first few minutes of T cell activation.
source: This mechanism of enhanced Notch processing peaks within the first few minutes of T cell activation.
evidence: This is supported by the time course data showing NICD nuclear accumulation at 5-20 min.

claim: 15 min of contact between a primed T cell and a professional APC is sufficient to trigger T cell proliferation 24 hr later.
source: 15 min of contact between a primed T cell and a professional APC is sufficient to trigger T cell proliferation 24 hr later (Iezzi et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: 1 hr of ZAP-70 activity can trigger substantial negative selection.
source: Similarly, 1 hr of ZAP-70 activity can trigger substantial negative selection (Au-Yeung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: 5 min of TGFβ incubation saturates Smad2 phosphorylation at 1 hr.
source: On an even shorter time scale 5 min of TGFβ incubation saturates Smad2 phosphorylation at 1 hr (Vizán et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: A single pulse of BCR engagement can trigger the nuclear accumulation of NFκB for 6 hr in B cells.
source: In B cells a single pulse of BCR engagement can trigger the nuclear accumulation of NFκB for 6 hr (Damdinsuren et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PKCθ deficiency in Tg4 mice resulted in a reduced number and proportion of CD4+ T cells.
source: As previously reported (Gupta et al., 2008; Sun et al., 2000) in non-TCR transgenic mouse strains, PKCθ deficiency in Tg4 mice resulted in a reduced number and proportion of CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2A and citations to prior work.

claim: The spreading of F-actin to the periphery of the interface was delayed in Tg4KO T cells.
source: The spreading of F-actin to the periphery of the interface was delayed in Tg4KO T cells (Figure 3D,E; Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3D,E.

claim: The interface diameter of Tg4KO T cells was significantly reduced across multiple time points.
source: The interface diameter of Tg4KO T cells was significantly (p<0.05) reduced across multiple time points (Figure 3F,G), as confirmed by electron microscopy (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging and electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The lamellum connecting the T cell body to the interface was smaller in Tg4KO T cells as it showed a significantly larger constriction or 'neck'.
source: The lamellum connecting the T cell body to the interface was smaller in Tg4KO T cells as it showed a significantly (p<0.001) larger constriction or 'neck' (Figure 3F,H).
evidence: This is supported by live cell imaging data shown in Figure 3F,H.

claim: Tg4KO T cells displayed modest defects across multiple elements of actin-driven cell spreading consistent with the slightly reduced efficiency of tight cell coupling.
source: Tg4KO T cells thus displayed modest defects across multiple elements of actin-driven cell spreading consistent with the slightly reduced efficiency of tight cell coupling.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on actin dynamics and cell coupling.

claim: Coronin activity is negatively regulated by serine/threonine phosphorylation, which can be induced by phorbol ester treatment.
source: Coronin activity is negatively regulated by serine/threonine phosphorylation, which can be induced by phorbol ester treatment (Cai et al., 2005; Oku et al., 2008, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: In AND T cells strong stimuli cause concerted accumulation of the TCR, Vav and Notch at the T cell/APC interface as related to efficient Notch activation.
source: In AND T cells strong stimuli cause concerted accumulation of the TCR, Vav and Notch at the T cell/APC interface as related to efficient Notch activation (Guy et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Actin dynamics may mediate coordinated interface accumulation of both ADAM10 and Notch.
source: Actin dynamics may thus mediate coordinated interface accumulation of both ADAM10 and Notch.
evidence: This is speculative, inferred from the data on actin-dependent ADAM10 recruitment and prior work on Notch accumulation.
